## Components

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    client["VPN client<br/>(Windows / macOS / iOS / Linux)"]

    subgraph edge["OpenSASE edge — one host or one compose network"]
        vpn["openvpn<br/>udp/5443<br/>TLS 1.2 · EC certs · tls-crypt"]
        dns["dnsmasq<br/>udp+tcp/53<br/>shared DNS for clients"]
        mitm["mitmproxy<br/>8080 explicit · TPROXY 80/443 transparent<br/>splice or bump per URL category<br/>clamd INSTREAM"]
        clam["clamav (clamd)<br/>tcp/3310<br/>verdicts"]
        log[("decisions.jsonl<br/>every verdict")]
    end

    net((Internet))

    client -- "OpenVPN" --> vpn
    vpn -- "DNS" --> dns
    vpn -- "HTTP/HTTPS" --> mitm
    mitm -- "INSTREAM scan" --> clam
    mitm -- "verdict" --> log
    mitm -- "clean" --> net
    mitm -. "INFECTED: blocked" .-> client

    style edge fill:transparent,stroke:#adb5bd
```

## Verdict pipeline

For every HTTP(S) request the mitmproxy addon evaluates, in order:

1. **passlist** hit → *splice* — the connection flows through untouched (no decrypt).
2. **bumplist** hit → *bump* — re-encrypt with the appliance CA, stream the payload to clamd via `INSTREAM`.
3. Neither → **default bump** (fail closed).
4. clamd returns **clean** → forwarded; **INFECTED** → connection blocked, verdict logged.

Every step writes one JSONL line: `{ts, host, url_category, action, verdict}` to `/data/log/decisions.jsonl` (containers) or `/var/lib/opensase/log/decisions.jsonl` (appliance).

## Component inventory

| Concern | Provided by |
|---|---|
| VPN | `services.openvpn` / `image-openvpn` (nixpkgs) |
| TLS inspection | mitmproxy addon — decrypt/re-encrypt on URL category |
| Malware scanning | clamd INSTREAM — the addon speaks the protocol directly |
| DNS | `services.dnsmasq` / `image-dnsmasq` |

One declarative source (`nix/images.nix` + `nix/appliance.nix`) drives both the
container images and the NixOS appliance; the Kubernetes base manifests render
from CUE (`k8s/manifests.cue`) against the same service model.

## Bill of materials

What the project is **built with** and what it **runs**, in one table. Runtime
picks are load-bearing for the verdict pipeline design; everything else is
plumbing chosen for declarativeness or supply-chain hygiene.

| Layer | Choice | Why this |
|---|---|---|
| **Runtime — edge** | OpenVPN (udp/5443, tls-crypt) | mature, client support everywhere, single UDP traversal |
| **Runtime — inspection** | mitmproxy + Python addon | programmatic splice/bump per request; INSTREAM clamd protocol natively |
| **Runtime — scanning** | ClamAV (clamd) | self-hostable signature engine, INSTREAM streaming scan |
| **Runtime — DNS** | dnsmasq | small, fits the appliance model; RPZ hook point for future DNS policy (#25) |
| **Declarative engine** | Nix flake (`flake.lock` pinned) | one source of truth for ALL artifacts below — images, appliance, manifests, PKI tooling |
| **Container images** | `dockerTools.buildLayeredImage` | hash-pinned layers, no Dockerfiles, no floating bases |
| **Appliance** | NixOS modules (`services.openvpn/dnsmasq/clamav/opensase`) | typed options, `nix flake check`-able, systemd-native TPROXY |
| **K8s manifests** | CUE → committed YAML (`nix run .#k8s-manifests`) | typed service model shared with images.nix; surfaces can't drift |
| **PKI** | easyRSA (vendored via Nix) + flake apps (`vpn-init`, `vpn-getclient`) | reproducible CA bootstrap + per-device client export |
| **CI** | GitHub Actions (flake-check, tests, release-images, pages) | signed-tag release pipeline; compose smoke gate before GHCR push |
| **Supply chain** | OpenSSF Scorecard + Best Practices, dependency-review, pre-commit.ci, GPG-signed commits/tags | repo hardening aligned with the release posture |
| **Docs site** | Quarto (`_quarto.yml`), mermaid diagrams, GitHub Pages | docs-as-code from the same repo; this page |
| **Tests** | pytest (addon unit + clamd env), compose smoke rehearsal | verdict pipeline behavior pinned in CI |

The rule of thumb: if it ships, it is a Nix derivation; if it is a choice, it
lives in the flake and is reviewable in one place.

## Transparent mode

`services.opensase.mitmMode = "transparent"` makes the appliance intercept ports 80/443 at the kernel with TPROXY (mangle table fwmark + policy routing), plus `ip_forward`. This never worked inside a Docker bridge; on NixOS it is a first-class systemd `preStart`, so it is reliable — at the cost of requiring the appliance to be the client's default gateway.

The GHCR/compose path ships the explicit-proxy mode (`8080`) which works everywhere a container can bind a port.
